run.question:
EU prod is having a checkout incident — 500s on POST /api/checkout. Investigate
using the app-267-prod-logs index.

report.summary: The incident is visible only in the `app-267-prod-logs` index, whose 4 documents in the authorized window all carry cluster=acme-prod-eu-west-1, region=eu-west-1, environment=prod: 3 ERROR and 1 WARN from checkout-service (2) and payment-service (2). The chain the logs state is: at 2026-11-23T15:55:52Z payment-service logged an upstream timeout calling `adyen-eu` `/v68/payments` after 30000ms and checkout-service logged `POST /api/checkout failed: payment provider response timeout after 30s (adyen-eu)`; at 16:55:52Z checkout-service logged `Circuit-breaker open for payment-service (failure rate 36%)`; at 17:25:52Z payment-service logged `adyen-eu degraded mode acknowledged via status page; retry queue depth=620`. The deepest observable origin of the checkout failures is therefore the external payment provider `adyen-eu`, which is not a Kubernetes object in this cluster (no service matching adyen/provider/psp exists; the only match was `image-provider`). The cluster itself shows no fault: all 24 deployments report ready replicas, checkout-6578865d87-v6flf and payment-6f7bc865d6-wwqnm are Running with restartCount 0, started 14:36Z, with a single ReplicaSet each created at 14:36Z (no rollout or restart in the window), no NetworkPolicies exist, and no fault-injection setting is on — every flag in the `flagd-config` ConfigMap (including paymentFailure and paymentUnreachable) has defaultVariant `off` and that ConfigMap's only recorded write is the Helm Apply at 14:36:29Z. Checkout and payment logs at 17:53-17:55Z show successful orders. Prometheus and Jaeger were unavailable in this Run, so the 500 rate, onset and recovery are unverified and the conclusion is partial.

claims.text: The `app-267-prod-logs` index contains exactly 4 documents in the authorized window, all with cluster=acme-prod-eu-west-1 and region=eu-west-1: service checkout-service 2 documents, service payment-service 2 documents; level ERROR 3, level WARN 1.
checkout-service logged at 2026-11-23T15:55:52Z, level ERROR, cluster acme-prod-eu-west-1: "POST /api/checkout failed: payment provider response timeout after 30s (adyen-eu)".
payment-service logged at 2026-11-23T15:55:52Z, level ERROR, cluster acme-prod-eu-west-1: "Upstream timeout calling adyen-eu /v68/payments after 30000ms".
checkout-service logged at 2026-11-23T16:55:52Z, level ERROR, cluster acme-prod-eu-west-1: "Circuit-breaker open for payment-service (failure rate 36%)".
payment-service logged at 2026-11-23T17:25:52Z, level WARN, cluster acme-prod-eu-west-1: "adyen-eu degraded mode acknowledged via status page; retry queue depth=620".
No Kubernetes service named or matching adyen, provider or psp exists across all namespaces: the only match was service image-provider in otel-demo; the cluster also holds 0 NetworkPolicies.
All 24 deployments in the cluster report ready and available replicas equal to spec.replicas, including otel-demo/checkout and otel-demo/payment at 1/1.

Pods checkout-6578865d87-v6flf, payment-6f7bc865d6-wwqnm and flagd-d6485586b-h9n2s are Running with restartCount 0 and startTime 2026-11-23T14:36:29-30Z, and each of checkout, payment and flagd has a single ReplicaSet (checkout-6578865d87, payment-6f7bc865d6, flagd-d6485586b) created 14:36Z with 1 replica, so no rollout or pod replacement occurred inside the incident window.

The flagd-config ConfigMap holds the fault-injection flags and both payment-related ones carry defaultVariant "off": paymentFailure ("Fail payment service charge requests n%", variants 100%/90%/75%/50%/25%/10%/off) and paymentUnreachable ("Payment service is unavailable"); all other flags (productCatalogFailure, recommendationCacheFailure, adManualGc, adHighCpu, adFailure, kafkaQueueProblems, cartFailure, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage, imageSlowLoad) also have defaultVariant "off".
The flagd-config ConfigMap was created 2026-11-23T14:36:29Z with resourceVersion 512 and its only recorded manager write is helm/Apply at 2026-11-23T14:36:29Z.

The checkout and payment deployment pod templates carry no provider or fault-injection env var: checkout has CHECKOUT_PORT, CART_ADDR, CURRENCY_ADDR, EMAIL_ADDR, PAYMENT_ADDR=payment:8080, PRODUCT_CATALOG_ADDR, SHIPPING_ADDR, FLAGD_HOST=flagd, FLAGD_PORT=8013; payment has PAYMENT_PORT and FLAGD_HOST/FLAGD_PORT only.

At the end of the window checkout and payment were succeeding: checkout-6578865d87-v6flf logged "[PlaceOrder] ..." followed by "payment went through (transaction_id: ...)" and "order confirmation email sent" at 17:55:03-17:55:50Z.

The payment-6f7bc865d6-wwqnm container's current log stream in the window contains only charge-received and transaction-complete info lines (15 newest of 210 lines, 17:53:24-17:55:50Z), each matching the checkout transactions.

The checkout 500s on POST /api/checkout originate in the external payment provider `adyen-eu`: payment-service's call to adyen-eu /v68/payments exceeded 30s and checkout-service's failed checkout line names the same provider timeout, followed by a provider degradation notice with a retry queue depth of 620. The 16:55:52Z circuit-breaker-open line (failure rate 36%) is consistent with checkout-service failing fast on payment-service while the provider stayed degraded; the share of 500 responses this explains is unverified because no HTTP status counts were obtainable.

A second open candidate is retry/queue amplification inside payment-service (retry queue depth=620 at 17:25:52Z and a 36% failure rate observed by checkout-service): retries against the slow provider could have prolonged checkout failures and re-opened the circuit breaker after adyen-eu recovered. No queue-depth series, error-rate series or trace data were available to test this.

Kubernetes faults were checked and not found as a cause of the checkout failures: all deployments hold their ready replicas, checkout/payment/flagd pods are Running with 0 restarts and were started at 14:36Z before the first error at 15:55:52Z, there is exactly one ReplicaSet per deployment from 14:36Z (no config-driven restart with an unchanged template during the window), and no NetworkPolicies exist that could block traffic.

Fault injection through flagd is not on as observed: paymentFailure and paymentUnreachable both have defaultVariant "off", every other flag is also "off", flagd-config has no recorded write after the helm Apply at 14:36:29Z, and the checkout and payment pod templates contain only FLAGD_HOST/FLAGD_PORT and no provider fault setting.

Confirm with the payment provider's status/incident record whether `adyen-eu` /v68/payments degraded around 2026-11-23T15:55Z and was still degraded at 17:25Z, and review payment-service retry/timeout settings (30s upstream timeout, retry queue depth 620) as advisory follow-up.

After the Prometheus and Jaeger backends for target m0-otel-20260909 are reachable again, measure checkout 5xx share for POST /api/checkout, payment-service error rate and adyen-eu client-call latency so the impact scope and recovery are verified rather than inferred from four log lines.

gaps: Prometheus was unreachable in this Run: get_metric_names, execute_prometheus_instant_query and metrics_range_query all returned status error/SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so no error-rate, latency or payment-transaction metric exists; the 500 rate, its onset and recovery are unverified and missing metric series are unknown, not zero.

Jaeger was unreachable: traces_list_services, traces_search and traces_search_by_tags returned status error/SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so there is no span-level evidence of which service or operation failed and no confirmed parent-child call edge between checkout, payment and adyen-eu.
The Kubernetes events query across all namespaces returned status no_data (0 events), so no rollout, kubelet or scheduling evidence exists; that absence is not proof nothing happened.
`app-267-prod-logs` holds only 4 documents in the window and none of them contains an HTTP status code, so the reported 500 responses and their count were not directly observed in logs.

The checkout pod log filter for error|fail|timeout|circuit|500|adyen and the payment pod log filter for error|fail|timeout|refus|circuit|adyen both returned status no_data (0 matching lines) over their read streams, and the frontend-proxy container returned no log bytes at all (status no_data), so edge-level and in-pod error text for the incident is unknown.

The flagd flag values in effect at 15:55:52Z are unknown: Kubernetes objects are current-state only and the change_history integration is not integrated, so a flag change and revert cannot be ruled out; the flagd container produced no log lines in the window (status no_data).

`adyen-eu` is an external dependency with no Kubernetes object and no reachable telemetry source in this Run; its own availability, latency and status-page record could not be read, so the provider-side cause rests on the two application log lines and the WARN status-page note, and the declared provider fault itself was not observed.

No previous container instance exists for checkout, payment or flagd, and logs older than the retained stream are unknown; the exact moment the provider degradation began and whether 500s were continuous between 15:55Z and 17:26Z are not observable from the retained data.
next_steps: Obtain the adyen-eu provider incident/status-page timeline for 2026-11-23 15:00-18:00Z to confirm the provider-side degradation window.
Once Prometheus/Jaeger are reachable, verify checkout POST /api/checkout 5xx ratio, payment-service error rate and adyen-eu client-call latency around 15:55Z, 16:55Z and 17:25Z.
Review payment-service retry-queue and circuit-breaker configuration (30s upstream timeout, retry queue depth 620) as advisory follow-up; no configuration change is proposed here.

view.cannot_prove: Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). <none> means the path reached no value in that object, not that the field is absent from the kind; a filtered table is not a full picture of the kind. When the API server returns zero objects of a kind other than events (every page read), the result is ok with total_items_processed 0: it proves only that there were no objects matching this kind, namespace and selectors at query time, not that none existed during the incident. Zero events, or a list your filter reduced to nothing, stays no_data. metadata.managedFieldsSummary gives each manager's last write time only: it is not a full change history (earlier writes by the same manager are gone) and it does not say which fields that write changed.
